en.headline: Maxim’s Palace opens seventh branch at MOKO in Mong Kok
en.dek: The new outlet retains traditional hand-pushed dim sum carts and adds live roast suckling pig carving and a dim sum academy for customers.
body: Maxim’s Group has opened the seventh branch of its Maxim’s Palace Chinese restaurant brand at MOKO shopping centre in Mong Kok.

The restaurant keeps the hand-pushed dim sum carts associated with traditional yum cha service. New features include an open kitchen where staff carve roast suckling pig in view of diners and a hands-on Maxim’s Dim Sum Academy. Classes teach two types of dim sum and are offered in Cantonese and English, with tuition starting at HK$450 per person.

The group said the branch aims to combine familiar tea-house elements with interactive experiences for modern diners. It is the first Maxim’s Chinese restaurant to present the roast pig carving in an open-kitchen setting.

zh.headline: 美心皇宮第七間分店進駐旺角MOKO
zh.dek: 新店保留人手推車點心傳統，新增現場燒乳豬切件及點心學堂體驗。
body: 美心集團旗下美心皇宮中菜品牌第七間分店已於旺角MOKO開業。
餐廳保留人手推車點心服務。新元素包括開放式廚房現場切燒乳豬，以及美心點心學堂。學堂每次教授兩款點心，設粵語及英語班，學費由每人450元起。
集團表示，新店結合茶樓傳統與互動體驗。這是美心中菜首次以開放式廚房形式展示燒乳豬切件。
